questions.notes: Highest on-time arrival rate among reporting airlines with at least 100 operated departures from DFW. The winner can be a regional affiliate. Reporting-carrier AA is not the American brand family.
questions.question: Which airline is most on time out of DFW?

       COUNT(*) AS n
FROM flights_v
WHERE operated AND origin = 'DFW'

HAVING COUNT(*) >= 100
ORDER BY on_time_rate DESC, label ASC

questions.notes: The gap is the morning on-time arrival rate minus the evening rate. Each bucket needs at least 500 operated departures. Largest means the most positive gap.
questions.question: Which airport has the largest morning-minus-evening on-time arrival gap?
questions.sql:
SELECT origin AS label,
       AVG(CASE WHEN dep_time_bucket = 'morning' THEN CASE WHEN on_time_arrival THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END END)
       - AVG(CASE WHEN dep_time_bucket = 'evening' THEN CASE WHEN on_time_arrival THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END END) AS rate_gap,
       COUNT(*) AS n
FROM flights_v
WHERE operated AND dep_time_bucket IN ('morning', 'evening')
GROUP BY origin
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN dep_time_bucket = 'morning' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) >= 500
   AND SUM(CASE WHEN dep_time_bucket = 'evening' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) >= 500
ORDER BY rate_gap DESC, label ASC
LIMIT 1

questions.notes: Directional, DFW to ORD. Both carriers are listed even if one has no flights. Rates are null when the operated count is zero, and those rates are not scored; the counts are. In this extract Southwest's Dallas flights use DAL, not DFW, so its DFW-ORD counts are the finding.
questions.question: How do American and Southwest compare on DFW to ORD? For each airline return scheduled flights and operated flights, plus the on-time arrival rate, cancellation rate, and average signed arrival delay when that airline flew the route.
questions.sql:
SELECT codes.airline_code AS label,
       COUNT(f.flight_date) AS scheduled_flights,
       COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN f.operated THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS operated_flights,
       AVG(CASE WHEN f.operated THEN CASE WHEN f.on_time_arrival THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END END) AS on_time_rate,
       AVG(CASE WHEN f.flight_date IS NOT NULL THEN CASE WHEN f.cancelled THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END END) AS cancellation_rate,
       AVG(CASE WHEN f.operated THEN f.arr_delay END) AS avg_arrival_delay
FROM (VALUES ('AA'), ('WN')) AS codes(airline_code)
LEFT JOIN flights_v f
  ON f.airline_code = codes.airline_code
 AND f.origin = 'DFW'
 AND f.dest = 'ORD'
GROUP BY codes.airline_code

questions.question: What is the passenger-weighted on-time arrival rate at ATL?

questions.notes: Departure metric, on the flights that have a departure delay. This is not the arrival standard.
questions.question: Rank the five most on-time airlines by on-time departure rather than arrival.
questions.sql:
SELECT airline_code AS label,
       AVG(CASE WHEN on_time_departure THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS on_time_departure_rate,
       COUNT(*) AS n
FROM flights_v
WHERE on_time_departure IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY airline_code
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5000
ORDER BY on_time_departure_rate DESC, label ASC
LIMIT 5

questions.notes: Overrides the operated-flight denominator. Every scheduled row is in the denominator. Only an arrival under 15 minutes counts as on time.
questions.question: What share of scheduled flights arrive on time if cancelled and diverted flights count as not on time?
questions.sql:
SELECT 'systemwide' AS label,
       AVG(CASE WHEN (NOT cancelled AND NOT diverted AND arr_delay < 15) THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS on_time_rate
FROM flights_v
WHERE TRUE

questions.notes: SkyWest flies for more than one major, so the draft family table leaves it out. The expected figure is 0.
questions.question: Is SkyWest part of the American single-partner family used in this project? Return 1 if it is and 0 if it is not.
questions.sql:
SELECT 'OO' AS label,
       CASE WHEN COUNT(*) > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS included
FROM carrier_families
WHERE family_code = 'AA' AND airline_code = 'OO'
